claim: PRC2 modifies chromatin by trimethylating lysine 27 on histone H3 (H3K27me3).
source: Repression of genes by Polycomb requires that PRC2 modifies their chromatin by trimethylating lysine 27 on histone H3 (H3K27me3).
evidence: This is a well-established fact stated in the abstract and supported by extensive literature in the field.

claim: Di- and tri-methylated H3K36 inhibit PRC2 at transcriptionally active genes.
source: At transcriptionally active genes, di- and tri-methylated H3K36 inhibit PRC2.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The cryo-EM structure of PRC2 on dinucleosomes reveals how binding of EZH2 to nucleosomal DNA orients the H3 N-terminus to place H3K27 into the active site.
source: Here, the cryo-EM structure of PRC2 on dinucleosomes reveals how binding of its catalytic subunit EZH2 to nucleosomal DNA orients the H3 N-terminus via an extended network of interactions to place H3K27 into the active site.
evidence: This claim is supported by the cryo-EM structural data presented in the manuscript, including Figure 1.

claim: Unmodified H3K36 occupies a critical position in the EZH2-DNA interface.
source: Unmodified H3K36 occupies a critical position in the EZH2-DNA interface.
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure showing the position of H3K36 in the interface.

claim: Mutation of H3K36 to arginine or alanine inhibits H3K27 methylation by PRC2 on nucleosomes in vitro.
source: Mutation of H3K36 to arginine or alanine inhibits H3K27 methylation by PRC2 on nucleosomes in vitro.
evidence: This is supported by HMTase assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Drosophila H3K36A and H3K36R mutants show reduced levels of H3K27me3.
source: Accordingly, Drosophila H3K36A and H3K36R mutants show reduced levels of H3K27me3 and defective Polycomb repression of HOX genes.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data and western blot analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: Drosophila H3K36A and H3K36R mutants show defective Polycomb repression of HOX genes.
source: Accordingly, Drosophila H3K36A and H3K36R mutants show reduced levels of H3K27me3 and defective Polycomb repression of HOX genes.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data showing HOX gene misexpression in Figure 6.

claim: The relay of interactions between EZH2, nucleosomal DNA and the H3 N-terminus creates the geometry that permits allosteric inhibition of PRC2 by methylated H3K36.
source: The relay of interactions between EZH2, the nucleosomal DNA and the H3 N-terminus therefore creates the geometry that permits allosteric inhibition of PRC2 by methylated H3K36 in transcriptionally active chromatin.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural and biochemical data presented in the manuscript.

claim: H3K27me3 marks chromatin for interaction with PRC1.
source: H3K27me3 marks chromatin for interaction with PRC1 (Fischle et al., 2003; Min et al., 2003), an effector which compacts chromatin (Francis et al., 2004; Grau et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PRC1 compacts chromatin.
source: H3K27me3 marks chromatin for interaction with PRC1 (Fischle et al., 2003; Min et al., 2003), an effector which compacts chromatin (Francis et al., 2004; Grau et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: H3K27me3 is recognized by PRC2 itself, and this interaction allosterically activates the PRC2 enzyme complex.
source: H3K27me3 is also recognized by PRC2 itself, and this interaction allosterically activates the PRC2 enzyme complex to facilitate deposition of H3K27me3 across extended domains of chromatin (Hansen et al., 2008; Margueron et al., 2009; Jiao and Liu, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: H3K4me3, H3K36me2, and H3K36me3 marks present on nucleosomes in transcriptionally active chromatin directly inhibit H3K27 methylation by PRC2.
source: In particular, the H3K4me3, H3K36me2, and H3K36me3 marks present on nucleosomes in transcriptionally active chromatin directly inhibit H3K27 methylation by PRC2 (Klymenko and Müller, 2004; Schmitges et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2011; Gaydos et al., 2012; Streubel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Inhibition of PRC2 by H3K4me3, H3K36me2, and H3K36me3 requires that these modifications are present in cis on the same H3 molecule containing the K27 substrate lysine.
source: Importantly, while stimulation of PRC2 activity by H3K27me3 acts in trans, inhibition of PRC2 by H3K4me3, H3K36me2, and H3K36me3 requires that these modifications are present in cis, that is, on the same H3 molecule containing the K27 substrate lysine (Schmitges et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2011; Voigt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: PRC2–DNA interactions make the largest contribution to the nucleosome-binding affinity of PRC2.
source: In particular, in nucleosome-binding assays, PRC2–DNA interactions make the largest contribution to the nucleosome-binding affinity of PRC2 (Wang et al., 2017; Choi et al., 2017) and H3K4me3, H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 do not seem to have a major effect on this binding affinity (Schmitges et al., 2011; Guidotti et al., 2019; Jani et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: H3K4me3, H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 do not have a major effect on PRC2 nucleosome-binding affinity.
source: In particular, in nucleosome-binding assays, PRC2–DNA interactions make the largest contribution to the nucleosome-binding affinity of PRC2 (Wang et al., 2017; Choi et al., 2017) and H3K4me3, H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 do not seem to have a major effect on this binding affinity (Schmitges et al., 2011; Guidotti et al., 2019; Jani et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: H3K4me3, H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 reduce the kcat of PRC2 for H3K27 methylation.
source: Instead, these three modifications were found to reduce the kcat of PRC2 for H3K27 methylation (Schmitges et al., 2011; Jani et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The PHF1-PRC2:di-Nuc cryo-EM reconstruction has an overall resolution of 5.2 Å.
source: Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy analysis yielded a reconstruction of the PHF1-PRC2:di-Nuc assembly with an overall resolution of 5.2 Å (Figure 1—figure supplement 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by the cryo-EM data processing results.

claim: The substrate nucleosome is bound by the EZH2CXC domain residues K563, Q565, K569 and Q570.
source: Specifically, the substrate nucleosome is bound by the EZH2CXC domain residues K563, Q565, K569 and Q570 (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 4A, cf. Poepsel et al., 2018), while the allosteric nucleosome is contacted by EED and by the SBD and SANT1 domains of EZH2 (Figure 1E, Poepsel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 4A.

claim: The allosteric nucleosome is contacted by EED and by the SBD and SANT1 domains of EZH2.
source: Specifically, the substrate nucleosome is bound by the EZH2CXC domain residues K563, Q565, K569 and Q570 (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 4A, cf. Poepsel et al., 2018), while the allosteric nucleosome is contacted by EED and by the SBD and SANT1 domains of EZH2 (Figure 1E, Poepsel et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The focused refinement on the interface of EZH2 and the substrate nucleosome yielded a map at 4.4 Å resolution.
source: Using particle signal subtraction and focused refinement on the interface of EZH2 and the substrate nucleosome (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 3), we then obtained an improved map at an apparent overall resolution of 4.4 Å which revealed well-defined density for the H3 N-terminus (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 3B–D).
evidence: This is directly stated and supported by the cryo-EM data processing results.

claim: The improved 4.4 Å map revealed well-defined density for the H3 N-terminus.
source: Using particle signal subtraction and focused refinement on the interface of EZH2 and the substrate nucleosome (Figure 1—figure supplement 2, Figure 1—figure supplement 3), we then obtained an improved map at an apparent overall resolution of 4.4 Å which revealed well-defined density for the H3 N-terminus (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 3B–D).
evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM density shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: A pseudo-atomic model of the histone H3 N-terminus spanning residues R26 to K37 was built.
source: The visible sidechain density combined with the crystallographic models of the PRC2 catalytic lobe and of the mononucleosome enabled us to build a pseudo-atomic model of the histone H3 N-terminus spanning residues R26 to K37 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by the model shown in Figure 1F.

claim: H3 R26 interacts with EZH2 Q648/D652.
source: This model revealed that EZH2 recognizes the H3 N-terminus via an extended network of contacts besides the previously described ionic interactions near the active site where H3 R26 interacts with EZH2 Q648/D652, and H3 K27 with the aromatic cage above the EZH2 catalytic center (Justin et al., 2016; Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by the structural model shown in Figure 1F and cited previous work.

claim: H3 K27 interacts with the aromatic cage above the EZH2 catalytic center.
source: This model revealed that EZH2 recognizes the H3 N-terminus via an extended network of contacts besides the previously described ionic interactions near the active site where H3 R26 interacts with EZH2 Q648/D652, and H3 K27 with the aromatic cage above the EZH2 catalytic center (Justin et al., 2016; Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by the structural model shown in Figure 1F and cited previous work.

claim: The structure suggests a hydrophobic hotspot involving H3 A29/P30 and EZH2 residues F667, A697, V699, I708 and F724.
source: Specifically, our structure suggests two hydrophobic hotspots, the first one involving H3 A29/P30 and EZH2 residues F667, A697, V699, I708 and F724 and the second one involving H3 V35 and F542, F557 and P558 of EZH2 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by the structural model shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The structure suggests a hydrophobic hotspot involving H3 V35 and EZH2 residues F542, F557 and P558.
source: Specifically, our structure suggests two hydrophobic hotspots, the first one involving H3 A29/P30 and EZH2 residues F667, A697, V699, I708 and F724 and the second one involving H3 V35 and F542, F557 and P558 of EZH2 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by the structural model shown in Figure 1F.

claim: H3 G33/G34 likely acts as a flexible hinge between the two hydrophobic interaction sites.
source: H3 G33/G34 is likely not recognized by PRC2 but might act as a flexible hinge between the two hydrophobic interaction sites (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural model shown in Figure 1F.

claim: H3K36 is directly juxtaposed to the EZH2CXC-DNA interaction surface.
source: H3K36 is directly juxtaposed to the EZH2CXC-DNA interaction surface and appears to be involved in the EZH2-DNA interface.
evidence: This is supported by the structural model shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The epsilon-amino group of H3K36 engages in a polar interaction with the carbonyl group of Q570.
source: The side-chain density of H3K36 suggests that the epsilon-amino group of H3K36 engages in a polar interaction with the carbonyl group of Q570 and possibly in long-range electrostatic interactions with the phosphate backbone of the nucleosomal DNA (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 4C–E).
evidence: This is supported by the structural model and density shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 4C–E.

claim: H3K36 possibly engages in long-range electrostatic interactions with the phosphate backbone of the nucleosomal DNA.
source: The side-chain density of H3K36 suggests that the epsilon-amino group of H3K36 engages in a polar interaction with the carbonyl group of Q570 and possibly in long-range electrostatic interactions with the phosphate backbone of the nucleosomal DNA (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 4C–E).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the structural model.

claim: A previously postulated H3K36-binding pocket centered on E579 of EZH2 is located approximately 19 Å away from H3K36 in the structure.
source: In this context, it should be noted that a previously postulated H3K36-binding pocket centered on E579 of EZH2 (Jani et al., 2019) is located approximately 19 Å away from H3K36 in our structure (Figure 1—figure supplement 4F).
evidence: This is supported by the structural model shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4F.

claim: An interaction of H3K36 with E579 of EZH2 as proposed by Muir and co-workers would require a very different binding geometry of PRC2 on the nucleosome.
source: An interaction of H3K36 with E579 of EZH2 as proposed by Muir and co-workers (Jani et al., 2019) would require a very different binding geometry of PRC2 on the nucleosome and major structural rearrangements of PRC2 or the nucleosome in order to avoid steric clashes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural data and comparison with a previous proposal.

claim: Wild-type PRC2 bound mononucleosomes with an apparent Kd in the mid-nanomolar range.
source: Wild-type PRC2 bound this mononucleosome with an apparent Kd in the mid-nanomolar range (Figure 2A,B, cf. Choi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: The binding affinities of PRC2CXC>A or PRC2EED>A were two- to three-fold lower than that of wild-type PRC2.
source: The binding affinities of PRC2CXC>A or PRC2EED>A were two- to three-fold lower than that of wild-type PRC2 and that of PRC2CXC>A/EED>A was about five-fold lower compared to the wild-type complex (Figure 2A,B, compare lanes 11–40 with 1–10).
evidence: This is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: The binding affinity of PRC2CXC>A/EED>A was about five-fold lower compared to the wild-type complex.
source: The binding affinities of PRC2CXC>A or PRC2EED>A were two- to three-fold lower than that of wild-type PRC2 and that of PRC2CXC>A/EED>A was about five-fold lower compared to the wild-type complex (Figure 2A,B, compare lanes 11–40 with 1–10).
evidence: This is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: The PRC2CXC>A/EED>A complex still binds to nucleosomes with sub-micromolar affinity.
source: The PRC2CXC>A/EED>A complex therefore still binds to nucleosomes with sub-micromolar affinity (Figure 2A, lanes 21–30).
evidence: This is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: PRC2CXC>A showed almost no detectable histone methyltransferase activity on mononucleosomes compared to wild-type PRC2.
source: On the same mononucleosomes used above, PRC2CXC>A showed almost no detectable histone methyltransferase (HMTase) activity compared to wild-type PRC2 (Figure 2C, compare lanes 5–7 with 2–4, see also Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by HMTase assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: On dinucleosomes, the PRC2CXC>A complex generates H3K27me1 and -me3 although much less efficiently than wild-type PRC2.
source: Indeed, on dinucleosomes, the PRC2CXC>A complex does generate H3K27me1 and -me3 although still much less efficiently than wild-type PRC2 (Figure 2C, compare lanes 12–14 with 9–11).
evidence: This is supported by HMTase assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: PRC2CXC>A did not show reduced K27 methylation activity compared to wild-type PRC2 on H3 peptide substrate.
source: However, it is important to note that PRC2CXC>A did not show reduced K27 methylation activity compared to wild-type PRC2 on this H3 peptide substrate (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry-based HMTase assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The mutations in the EZH2CXC domain do not appear to alter the conformation of EZH2 in a way that would directly interfere with catalysis.
source: The mutations in the EZH2CXC domain therefore do not appear to alter the conformation of EZH2 in a way that would directly interfere with catalysis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the peptide HMTase assay data.

claim: Interaction of the EZH2CXC domain with the DNA on the substrate nucleosomes is a critical step for engaging the H3 N-terminus in a manner that allows effective H3K27 methylation.
source: Taken together, these observations strongly argue for a mechanism where interaction of the EZH2CXC domain with the DNA on the substrate nucleosomes is a critical step for engaging the H3 N-terminus in a manner that allows effective H3K27 methylation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutational and biochemical data.

claim: The affinity of PRC2 for binding to mononucleosomes containing H3Kc36me3 was indistinguishable from that for binding to unmodified mononucleosomes.
source: In EMSAs, the affinity of PRC2 for binding to mononucleosomes containing a trimethyllysine analog at H3K36 (H3Kc36me3) (Simon et al., 2007) was indistinguishable from that for binding to unmodified mononucleosomes (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: On H3Kc36me3-containing mononucleosomes, H3K27 mono- and trimethylation by PRC2 was more than 10-fold inhibited.
source: As previously reported (Schmitges et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2011), on H3Kc36me3-containing mononucleosomes, H3K27 mono- and trimethylation by PRC2 was more than 10-fold inhibited (Figure 3C, compare lanes 5–7 with 2–4, see also Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by HMTase assay data shown in Figure 3C and cited previous work.

claim: Methylation of H3K27 was inhibited on mononucleosomes where H3K36 had been mutated to arginine (H3K36R).
source: Methylation of H3K27 was also inhibited on mononucleosomes where H3K36 had been mutated to arginine (H3K36R) and, intriguingly, also on H3K36A mononucleosomes (Figure 3C, compare lanes 8–13 with 2–4).
evidence: This is supported by HMTase assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Methylation of H3K27 was inhibited on H3K36A mononucleosomes.
source: Methylation of H3K27 was also inhibited on mononucleosomes where H3K36 had been mutated to arginine (H3K36R) and, intriguingly, also on H3K36A mononucleosomes (Figure 3C, compare lanes 8–13 with 2–4).
evidence: This is supported by HMTase assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: PRC2 inhibition on H3K36R and H3K36A mononucleosomes was less severe than on H3Kc36me3 mononucleosomes.
source: PRC2 inhibition on H3K36R and H3K36A mononucleosomes was less severe than on H3Kc36me3 mononucleosomes (Figure 3C, compare lanes 8–13 with 5–7).
evidence: This is supported by HMTase assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: On free H3 peptide, H3K36me3 did not inhibit H3K27 monomethylation by PRC2.
source: Importantly, on this free H3 peptide, H3K36me3 did not inhibit H3K27 monomethylation by PRC2 (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry-based HMTase assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The allosteric inhibition of PRC2 by H3K36me3 only occurs in the context of the geometric constraints of the nucleosome.
source: The allosteric inhibition of PRC2 by H3K36me3 therefore only occurs in the context of the geometric constraints of the nucleosome.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of nucleosome and peptide HMTase assays.

claim: DNA-binding by the winged-helix domain of PHF1 increases the binding affinity and residence time of PHF1-PRC2 on nucleosomes about two- to three-fold.
source: DNA-binding by the winged-helix domain of PHF1 increases the binding affinity and residence time of PHF1-PRC2 on nucleosomes about two- to three-fold, resulting in more efficient H3K27 methylation by this complex compared to PRC2 (Choi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: H3K27 mono- and tri-methylation by PHF1-PRC2 was strongly inhibited on H3Kc36me3 mononucleosomes.
source: H3K27 mono- and tri-methylation by PHF1-PRC2 was strongly inhibited on H3Kc36me3 mononucleosomes (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by HMTase assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: H3K36me3 inhibits H3K27 methylation by PHF1-PRC2 even though this complex has higher binding affinity and a prolonged residence time on nucleosomes.
source: H3K36me3 therefore inhibits H3K27 methylation by PHF1-PRC2 even though this complex has higher binding affinity and a prolonged residence time on nucleosomes (Choi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the HMTase assay data and cited previous work.

claim: H3K36R mutant animals complete embryogenesis and their cuticle morphology is indistinguishable from wildtype.
source: Using the H3K36R strain from Matera and colleagues (McKay et al., 2015), we found that H3K36R mutant animals complete embryogenesis and that their cuticle morphology is indistinguishable from wildtype (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by cuticle analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: 81% of H3K36R mutant animals arrested development at variable time points during larval growth.
source: Specifically, 81% of H3K36R mutant animals arrested development at variable time points during larval growth, 18% developed to the end of third larval instar and formed pupae that died prior to metamorphosis, and 1% developed into late pupae that complete metamorphosis but then arrested as pharate adults (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by developmental analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: 18% of H3K36R mutant animals developed to the end of third larval instar and formed pupae that died prior to metamorphosis.
source: Specifically, 81% of H3K36R mutant animals arrested development at variable time points during larval growth, 18% developed to the end of third larval instar and formed pupae that died prior to metamorphosis, and 1% developed into late pupae that complete metamorphosis but then arrested as pharate adults (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by developmental analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: 1% of H3K36R mutant animals developed into late pupae that complete metamorphosis but then arrested as pharate adults.
source: Specifically, 81% of H3K36R mutant animals arrested development at variable time points during larval growth, 18% developed to the end of third larval instar and formed pupae that died prior to metamorphosis, and 1% developed into late pupae that complete metamorphosis but then arrested as pharate adults (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by developmental analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: H3K36R mutant pharate adults consistently showed homeotic transformations reminiscent of polycomb group mutants.
source: When we dissected the rare H3K36R mutant pharate adults from their pupal cases and examined their epidermal structures, we found that they consistently showed homeotic transformations reminiscent of polycomb group (PcG) mutants.
evidence: This is supported by phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: PcG mutant phenotypes in H3K36R mutants included antenna-to-leg transformations and extra sex comb teeth on meso- and meta-thoracic legs in males.
source: These PcG mutant phenotypes included antenna-to-leg transformations and extra sex comb teeth on meso- and meta-thoracic legs in males (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: 98% of H3K36R mutant animals (from the strain constructed in this study) arrested development at the end of embryogenesis.
source: However, 98% of individuals arrested development already at the end of embryogenesis and the 2% of mutant animals that hatched from the eggshell arrested development as first instar larvae (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by developmental analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: 96% of H3K36A mutant animals arrested development before hatching from the eggshell.
source: 96% of these H3K36A mutant animals arrested development before hatching from the eggshell and the 4% that hatched died during the first larval instar (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by developmental analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 bulk levels were reduced more than 4-fold in H3K36R mutant larvae compared to wildtype.
source: We first performed western blot analyses on H3K36R mutant larvae and found that H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 bulk levels were reduced more than 4-fold compared to wildtype (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: H3K36R mutant animals showed an about two-fold reduction in H3K27me3 bulk levels compared to wildtype.
source: Intriguingly, H3K36R mutant animals also showed an about two-fold reduction in H3K27me3 bulk levels compared to wildtype (Figure 5A, compare lanes 4–6 with 1–3).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In H3K36A mutants, H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 bulk levels were reduced about 3- to 4-fold compared to wildtype.
source: In H3K36A mutants, H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 bulk levels were reduced about 3- to 4-fold compared to wildtype (Figure 5B, compare lanes 5–8 with 1–4).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In both H3K36A and H3K36R mutant embryos, H3K27me3 bulk levels appeared largely unchanged compared to wildtype.
source: In both genotypes, H3K27me3 bulk levels appeared largely unchanged compared to wildtype (Figure 5B, compare lanes 5–8 and 9–12 with 1–4).
evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: H3K36me2 levels across the genome were strongly diminished in H3K36R mutant larvae.
source: As expected from the western blot analyses (Figure 5A), H3K36me2 levels across the genome were strongly diminished in H3K36R mutant larvae (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The levels of H3K27me3 were considerably reduced in the chromatin of late-stage H3K36R mutant larvae.
source: The H3K27me3 genomic profile confirmed that the levels of this modification were considerably reduced in the chromatin of late-stage H3K36R mutant larvae (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: H3K27me3 levels were particularly strongly diminished at canonical PRC2 target genes such as the HOX genes in H3K36R mutant larvae.
source: While the average reduction was only about two-fold (Figure 5C), H3K27me3 levels were particularly strongly diminished at canonical PRC2 target genes such as the HOX genes that in wildtype animals are decorated with high-levels of H3K27me3 (Figure 5C,E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5C,E.

claim: At the HOX genes Ubx, abd-A, Abd-B or Antp, H3K27me3 levels in H3K36R mutants were between three and fourfold lower than in wildtype.
source: Specifically, at the HOX genes Ultrabithorax (Ubx), abdominal-A (abd-A), Abdominal-B (Abd-B) or Antennapedia (Antp), H3K27me3 levels in H3K36R mutants were between three and fourfold lower than in wildtype (Figure 5C,E).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5C,E.

claim: In both H3K36A and H3K36R mutant embryos, H3K27me3 levels were about 1.5-fold reduced across the HOX gene loci.
source: However, in both mutants, H3K27me3 levels were about 1.5-fold reduced across the HOX gene loci (Figure 5D,F).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5D,F.

claim: Both H3K36R and H3K36A mutants showed stochastic misexpression of Abd-B in single cells or pairs of cells in the CNS of late-stage embryos.
source: Both mutants showed stochastic misexpression of Abd-B in single cells or pairs of cells in the CNS of late-stage embryos (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Abd-B misexpression in H3K36R and H3K36A mutant embryos was less widespread than in H3K27R mutant embryos or in embryos lacking the PRC2 subunit Esc.
source: Abd-B misexpression in H3K36R and H3K36A mutant embryos was however clearly less widespread than in H3K27R mutant embryos or in embryos lacking the PRC2 subunit Esc that are shown for comparison (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: In the CNS of every single H3K36R mutant individual, Ubx was widely misexpressed in many single cells in an apparently stochastic pattern.
source: In the CNS of every single mutant individual, Ubx was widely misexpressed in many single cells in an apparently stochastic pattern (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: 50% of the H3K36R mutant larvae showed stochastic misexpression of Ubx in individual cells in the wing blade primordium of the wing imaginal disc.
source: 50% of the H3K36R mutant larvae also showed stochastic misexpression of Ubx in individual cells in the wing blade primordium of the wing imaginal disc (Figure 6C), the area of this disc where Ubx is most readily de-repressed if PcG function is perturbed (Beuchle et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: 100% of the H3K36R mutant larvae showed misexpression of Antp in the antenna primordium of the eye-anntennal disc.
source: Finally, we found that 100% of the H3K36R mutant larvae showed misexpression of Antp in the antenna primordium of the eye-anntennal disc (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Antp misexpression was observed in clones of H3K36A homozygous cells.
source: We also observed this misexpression in clones of H3K36A homozygous cells that we had induced in H3K36A heterozygous animals (Figure 6D) and in H3K27R mutant clones that were induced as control (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The stochastic misexpression of multiple HOX genes in animals with chromatin consisting of H3K36R or H3K36A nucleosomes is caused by defective Polycomb repression as a result of the reduced H3K27me3 levels in HOX gene chromatin.
source: The most straightforward explanation for the stochastic misexpression of multiple HOX genes in animals with chromatin consisting of H3K36R or H3K36A nucleosomes therefore is that it is caused by defective Polycomb repression as a result of the reduced H3K27me3 levels in HOX gene chromatin.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined genetic and molecular data.

claim: Different forms of PRC2 use the same molecular interactions for binding the H3 N-terminus on substrate nucleosomes.
source: Consistent with our findings here, an independent recent study of a cryo-EM structure of PRC2 with co-factors JARID2 and AEBP2 bound to a mononucleosome with monoubiquitylated H2A (Kasinath et al., 2020) identified very similar interactions of EZH2 with the nucleosomal DNA and the H3 N-terminus.
evidence: This is supported by comparison with an independent study.

claim: Unmodified H3K36 has the right fit for interaction of the H3 N-terminus with the EZH2 surface and placement of H3K27 in the active site.
source: Unmodified H3K36 has the right fit for interaction of the H3 N-terminus with the EZH2 surface and placement of H3K27 in the active site.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural and biochemical data.

claim: H3K36me2/3, H3K36R or H3K36A alterations of the side chain of residue 36 in H3 impair productive interaction of H3K27 with the catalytic center of EZH2.
source: The inhibition of H3K27 mono-, di- and tri-methylation on nucleosomes carrying H3K36me2 or -me3 (Schmitges et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2011) or on H3K36R or H3K36A nucleosomes (Figure 3C) suggests that even though these side chains could theoretically be accommodated in the EZH2CXC-DNA interface, these alterations of the side chain of residue 36 in H3 chain must somehow impair productive interaction of H3K27 with the catalytic center of EZH2.
evidence: This is an inference based on the biochemical data.

claim: Docking of the H3K36 side chain in the EZH2CXC-DNA interface is critical for rapid alignment of the H3 N-terminus on the EZH2 surface into a catalytically competent state.
source: Taken together, a possible scenario would therefore be that within the time frame of the PRC2-nucleosome binding and reaction cycle, docking of the H3K36 side chain in the EZH2CXC-DNA interface is critical for rapid alignment of the H3 N-terminus on the EZH2 surface into a catalytically competent state.
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed to explain the data.

claim: H3K36me2/3 does not locally disrupt nucleosome binding but allosterically inhibits H3K27 from interacting with the EZH2 active site.
source: According to this view, H3K36me2/3 does not locally disrupt nucleosome binding but allosterically inhibits H3K27 from interacting with the EZH2 active site.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the data.

claim: PRC2 is unable to effectively deposit high levels of H3K27me3 on the H3K36R or H3K36A nucleosomes in Drosophila chromatin.
source: A simple straightforward explanation for these phenotypes in H3K36R or H3K36A mutant animals is that PRC2 is unable to effectively deposit high levels of H3K27me3 on the H3K36R or H3K36A nucleosomes, respectively, in their chromatin.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vivo genetic and molecular data.

claim: H3K27me3 levels at HOX genes are below the threshold needed to stringently maintain Polycomb repression in H3K36R or H3K36A mutants, causing stochastic misexpression.
source: Accordingly, H3K27me3 levels at HOX genes are below the threshold needed to stringently maintain Polycomb repression and consequently, HOX genes become stochastically misexpressed in a fraction of cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genetic and molecular data.

claim: It is the exquisite geometry formed by a relay of interactions between the PRC2 enzyme, nucleosomal DNA and the H3 N-terminus that enable H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 to allosterically prevent PRC2 from depositing H3K27me3 at transcribed genes.
source: The structural, biochemical and genetic work reported in this study shows that it is the exquisite geometry formed by a relay of interactions between the PRC2 enzyme, nucleosomal DNA and the H3 N-terminus that enable the histone methylation marks H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 in transcriptionally active chromatin to allosterically prevent PRC2 from depositing the repressive histone methylation mark H3K27me3 at transcribed genes.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, integrating all the data.
